findings.title: First uniform dispatch accepts a corrupted positive worker sample count
findings.reproduction: reviewer_candidate_probes.py::count_probe: real max_concurrency child trains a 2-item sampler, saves the valid endpoint/history/token bundle, then changes only worker-state num_samples from 2 to 3. On its first uniform dispatch expected_count_or_null is None.
findings.observed: Both Python versions accept the parent result, emit report/payload count 3, and server commits round1 with observed_counts={1:3}; actual sampler cardinality is 2. Cloud remains correctly 1.433, so this is count provenance/acceptance failure, not an incorrect gradient claim. The identical corruption is rejected in sample mode.
findings.cause: Worker count is compared only with a previously known/configured dispatch count. No independent current-attempt realized count binds first uniform parent handoff; report count is then overwritten with the sidecar value.
findings.required_behavior: Bind and validate the current realized partition count in the parent before accepting the sidecar/outbound result. Wrong worker count must roll back and send no update, including when the server had no previous count.

findings.title: Resume accepts loss of the count cache for a client with nonzero history
findings.reproduction: reviewer_candidate_probes.py::bundle_count_probe: commit clients1 and2 with counts2 each, save the real round2 bundle, remove only counts[1] while retaining nonzero history1 and all model/config/RNG/token fields, and load fresh objects. Dispatch client1 with a now-3-item partition.
findings.observed: Both versions accept the incomplete bundle, dispatch client1 with expected_count_or_null=None, accept its changed count3 and commit round3. Persisted h1 is approximately -0.378, proving it was previously trained and needed its realized count binding.
findings.cause: Validation checks present count entries and only requires a nonempty map at positive rounds. It does not reject a missing count for a client whose saved history proves prior participation.
findings.required_behavior: Reject this inconsistent bundle before changing live/pending state. Preserve fixed-data count provenance through continuation; at minimum a nonzero stored history must have a validated observed count.

findings.title: Receive callback can commit an invalid boolean inactive count
findings.reproduction: reviewer_callback_count_probe.py: commit client2 at count1. During the next valid client1 round, on_weights_received changes only inactive observed_counts[2] from int1 to boolTrue.
findings.observed: Both versions commit round2 with observed_counts[2] of type bool. Subsequent save_to_checkpoint raises "FedDyn checkpoint sample count must be a positive integer." Previous canonical bytes remain at round1; live model/history/round have advanced.
findings.cause: Python dictionary equality treats 1 and True as equal, bypassing the precommit authority guard. Staging preserves the invalid inactive entry; count validity is checked only during later bundle validation.
findings.required_behavior: Use type-sensitive comparison/validation for FedDyn-owned count state before arithmetic/commit. Reject and roll back this owned-state mutation; no arbitrary external callback side-effect transaction is requested.
